title: RaW Sounds Today: Only The Poets, Storm Deva, Asteroid Lily
excerpt: Each week we like to champion the music scene with ten songs in our playlist that all have a connection
content:
Each week we like to champion the music scene with ten songs in our playlist that all have a connection to the RaW (Reading and Wokingham) area and sometimes beyond. We’ve got three new entries this week, connected with the area. As always, we have a wide variety of musical styles, but we think they’re all worth a listen and we hope you find something new to enjoy as well as maybe getting out to experience the thrill of live music.

1. Only The Poets – Emotional –

Reading’s own Only The Poets have been having a fantastic year, with a Top 10 album and sold-out Reading and London gigs earlier this year. They’re currently in the middle of a European tour, but didn’t forget their home town, with a visit to Sub89 (which still attracted fans from further afield, some of the front row had come from Germany!). They picked The Ariston (who have graced the stage at Wokingham Festival a couple of times) to open for them, and then delivered a show to delight their fans, ending with Emotional, which has particular local significance as it’s inspired by an encounter at The Purple Turtle. https://www.facebook.com/onlythepoets

2. Storm Deva – Carpe Diem –

Storm Deva appeared at Wokingham Festival a few years ago and they performed a wonderful set as a duo comprising Carollyn Eden on vocals/keyboards plus Stuart Clark on guitars. They certainly had atmosphere and melody with their blend of emotive classic and progressive rock. Their live performances have now been enhanced even further as Carollyn and Stuart have added other good musicians around them to create a full band. They describe themselves as a cinematic rock band with a big dynamic sound and we’ve heard very positive reports about their latest incarnation. It’s therefore great to hear that they will be at The Butler in Reading on December 8th where they will be supported by Daughter of the Water who we’ve seen a few times before. They are always good so, with two quality acts on the bill, it should be an excellent night of quality music. This track is taken from Storm Deva’s self titled debut album – https://www.stormdeva.com

3. Asteroid Lily – You & I –

We caught Asteroid Lily at the Purple Turtle in June, courtesy of Radio Wigwam. They return to Reading as part of the XOX Project (based around vintage Roland synths) from Readipop, at the Oakford Social Club on 26th November. This, their latest single, is lovely piece of electro pop that examines a relationship where the reality did not match the dreams promised at the outset, and how hard it is to say goodbye. https://www.asteroidlily.com/

4. Millie Manders and the Shutup – Age Disgracefully –

We featured Millie Manders and the Shutup early in the year after their appearance at last year’s Reading Rising (this year’s has just finished, and it was as excellent as ever), and they returned to the Face Bar for Future Transmissions and put on another exemplary show. This is their latest single, which the crowd all joined in with joyfully, a great protest against society’s pressures to be forever young. https://www.facebook.com/milliemandersmusic

5. Radiator – Sunday –

Radiator are from London, but we’ve seen them play two very good sets down at the Purple Turtle, with vocalist Ollie prowling round the stage. This is their latest single, and their most recent appearance was part of a tour promoting it, and it deservedly got into the vinyl singles charts. https:// www.instagram.com/radiatorbanduk

6. Áine Deane – EARN LOVE –

We’ve followed Áine Deane for some time, as Chris’s daughter was at university with her (and even featured on one of her singles), and we really enjoyed her appearance at Wokingham Festival headlining on the second stage in 2024. This is her most recent single, from her to be loved by a songwriter EP, and is an optimistic song about finding a genuine uncontrolling love. https:// www.facebook.com/ainedeanemusic

7. Little Red – Dusk –

Another new band to us, but one which has been around the area for a while; we saw that Little Red would be appearing at The Rising Sun Arts Centre, and listened to a couple of tracks, and enjoyed what we heard, so went along and had a great time listening to their dark alt-folk songs. Little Red have returned with new material after a hiatus caused by real life events, some of which have informed the new tracks, and they are definitely worth seeing live. https://www.facebook.com/littleredband

8. David J – Requiem for the Rose Garden –

David J was co-founder, bass player and joint songwriter in Bauhaus (best known for “Bela Lugosi’s Dead”) and Love and Rockets; this is a track from his forthcoming new album Postcards from the Afterlife, a protest song about the literal and metaphorical destruction wrought by the current incumbent of the White House. You can see David J perform live at the Face Bar on 2nd December, courtesy of Future Transmissions. https://www.facebook.com/mcnightshade

9. Ro Jordan – sirens –

We saw Ro Jordan at Wokingham Festival and at the Purple Turtle this year, both courtesy of Radio Wigwam. She’s just released this, her latest single, about the experience of waking up to the sound of sirens and the person who stayed with her through the emergency. It’s full of beautiful harmonies, and is about the strength of the support overcoming the situation. https://www.instagram.com/rojordanofficial/

10. Sundaughter – Silver –

We featured Sundaughter last year, and said we’d be looking to check them out. We did just that, seeing them at The Butler, then support Pale Blue Eyes at South Street Arts, and then on the main stage at Down At The Abbey, and we liked what we saw. This is their latest single, a shimmering piece of shoegaze with dreamy vocals. They are playing a run of gigs in London and Bristol over the next few weeks, see their socials for details. https://www.instagram.com/sundaughterband/

You can listen to all the songs featured in our Spotify playlist at https://bit.ly/rawsoundstoday
